answer: A falcon-inspired reputation system can resist sybil attacks by tying each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history. Like a crystal that only forms under sustained pressure, trust grows only after many successful, attested interactions over time. New identities start with zero reputation and must earn it slowly, while a cipher-based proof-of-work makes creating each fake account expensive in compute. An attacker would need to pay the work cost for thousands of identities and then invest weeks building fake histories, which makes large-scale sybil farming unprofitable.
